topSignals.title: Bloom Energy Q1 2026: Revenue +130% YoY, FY guidance raised to $3.4–3.8B
topSignals.text: — Q1 revenue $751M (product revenue +208% YoY); non-GAAP gross margin 31.5%; adjusted EBITDA $143M; operating cash flow $73.6M. Full-year guidance implies ~80% YoY growth at midpoint.

topSignals.title: Oracle Project Jupiter: 2.45 GW Bloom fuel cell campus in New Mexico
topSignals.text: — Oracle, BorderPlex Digital Assets, and Bloom Energy confirmed Project Jupiter will run entirely on Bloom fuel cells, replacing previously planned gas turbines and diesel generators. Single largest announced fuel cell data center installation globally. Initial 1.2 GW contracted; full 2.45 GW targeting 2027 completion.

topSignals.title: FuelCell Energy exits SOFC market, takes $64.5M impairment; launches 12.5 MW MCFC data center power block
topSignals.text: — Strategic pivot away from solid oxide technology; FCEL stock fell ~10% in early June on the news (trading ~$22). Company redirects focus to molten carbonate fuel cells and new packaged 12.5 MW utility-grade power block product targeting data centers.

items.text: Ceres Power new 10.8 kW solid oxide stack — Unveiled for data center on-site power and green hydrogen production, positioned as modular buildingblock for large installations. Centrica partnership (signed March 2026) explores natural-gas-fuelled SOFC for European data centres and industrial sites.
Elcogen factory output — Tallinn factory (opened Sept 2025) reporting degradation <0.3%/1,000 h via gadolinium-doped ceria layers; 10-year warranties becoming market differentiator.
Sunfire pressurized reversible stacks — 10–30 bar operation improves round-trip efficiency by up to 12 percentage points; reduces balance-of-plant footprint, relevant for data center CHP.
FuelCell Energy exits SOFC — $64.5M impairment; market consolidates further around Bloom Energy and Ceres/licensees. FCEL pivots to MCFC 12.5 MW block product.

Oracle + Bloom 2.8 GW strategic partnership (April 13–27) — 1.2 GW contracted, deployment underway through 2027; Project Jupiter (New Mexico) is anchor deployment at 2.45 GW. Bloom stock +22% on announcement day.
Bloom + AEP: $2.65B, up to 1 GW — Q1 2026 contract for utility-scale SOFC behind-the-meter deployments.
Bloom + Brookfield: $5B global partnership — Late 2025 deal; Bloom targeting 2 GW/yr manufacturing capacity by end-2026 (up from 1 GW).
Bloom + Equinix: 100 MW+ across 19 data centers — Ongoing deployment programme across colocation sites.
FuelCell Energy + SDCL: 450 MW pipeline — January 2026 strategic partnership to jointly develop up to 450 MW of fuel cell power systems for data centers.
Survey: 32% of US data centers plan full off-grid SOFC by 2030 — Bloom Energy 2026 Data Center Power Report. Reflects accelerating behind-the-meter trend driven by grid queue delays.
Quiet day — no new regulatory/policy items since June 10.

Gas turbine capex still elevated — Construction costs up ~66% over two years (material/labour inflation from data center demand surge); delays in large gas turbine orders continue to benefit SOFC competitiveness on installed cost per kW.
FuelCell Energy's MCFC 12.5 MW block product enters as new competing on-site option; direct competition with Bloom's Energy Server at equivalent power scales.
Bloom Energy (BE): Q1 2026 revenue $751M (+130% YoY), FY guidance $3.4–3.8B. Non-GAAP EPS guidance $1.85–$2.25. Stock surged ~22% on Oracle deal (April 14).
FuelCell Energy (FCEL): Stock down ~10% in early June to ~$22; Q4 FY2025 revenue $55M (+12% YoY); backlog $1.24B; cash $278M. SOFC exit weighing on sentiment.
Ceres Power: ~£45M contracted revenue for 2026; licensing model validated by Doosan Fuel Cell mass production.
SOFC market 2026: ~$2.89B globally, projected $16.53B by 2031. SOFC holds 47.8% of fuel cell data center market share.
Ceres 10.8 kW stack — new product release demonstrates continued IP-protected stack scaling; aiming to cut green hydrogen production costs alongside data center power.

lcoe.text: LCOE at current NG prices (~$3.34/MMBtu): Bottom of the $130–205/MWh range applies (~$130/MWh unsubsidized, lower with ITC 48E). CHP-adjusted (with heat credit) can reach $120/MWh.
Fuel cell data center market size 2026: $361M; forecast $1.19B by 2033 (CAGR 18.6%).
FuelCell Energy 12.5 MW block: packaged product; capex/MW economics TBD but targeting utility-grade cost competitiveness.
Manufacturing scale-up: Bloom doubling to 2 GW/yr; FCEL expanding CT plant from ~100 to 350 MW — both should pressure $/kW downward through 2026–2027.
